To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the glass transition temperature of thin supported polymer films is lower than that of bulk polymer films, and this difference increases with decreasing film thickness and (2) the glass transition dynamics of thin supported polymer film are enhanced by the enhanced mobility of the free surface.
the dynamics of entangled polystystyrene films of various thicknesses and molecular weight deviate from bulk behavior at the temperature T(*) =Tg + 6K = 380 K ± 1 K.

thin films of entangled polystystyrene show a temperature, T(*), below which the dynamics are facilitated by enhanced mobility at the surface, and that the relaxation dynamics slow down slightly as molecular weight increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics in entangled polystystrene thin films.
the relaxation dynamics of entangled polymer thin films, and the effect of the free surface on those dynamics.
the dynamics of supported polymer films, which have been shown to be of great importance in a wide range of fields, from adhesives and coatings to the development of polymer-based electronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dynamics of entangled polymer thin films are facilitated by the free surface and that the dynamics of the film are not affected by the presence of the substrate.
thin films of entangled polymers exhibit a reduction in Tg and an enhancement of dynamics near the free surface, which can be attributed to the enhanced mobility of the free surface.
the glass transition in entangled polymer thin films is not a bulk property and that its dynamics are facilitated by free surface mobility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the relaxation dynamics in supported thin films of entangled polystystyrene is facilitated by the enhanced dynamics at the free surface, but that this enhancement is partially suppressed by entanglements.
the glass transition of entangled supported polymer films is facilitated by the enhanced free surface dynamics.
the dynamics of entangled polymer films are facilitated by enhanced dynamics near the free surface and that the effect of the substrate is not as strong as previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
supported polymer thin films can be used to probe the interfacial dynamics of bulk polymer systems.

thin films of entangled polymers have a unique temperature T(*) at which their dynamics deviate from bulk behavior, and this deviation is caused by the enhanced mobility of polymer chains at the free surface of the film.

the glass transition temperature and relaxation dynamics of thin films of entangled polymers can be strongly influenced by the presence of free surfaces, and the effect of free surfaces can be observed at temperatures as high as ∼20 K below the Tg of the bulk polymer.
